issue.title: Retire epic_resume_gate
issue.description: Opt-in beta: the epic_resume chop raises an EpicResume gate when a failed phase agent stalls an epic.

task_type_fields.remove_when: The chop has gated real stalls without false positives on handoff races or fast retries at the configured `bead.epic_resume.settle_seconds`.
task_type_fields.when_disabled: A stalled epic raises no gate; recovery is entirely manual through `sase bead work <epic-id>`.
task_type_fields.when_enabled: The `epic_resume` chop raises an `EpicResume` gate when a failed phase agent has stalled an epic.

payload.entry:
PROVENANCE: this bead replaces sase-pa, the `flag`-issue-type bead that owned `epic_resume_gate` from its creation at 2026-08-18T03:19:01Z by bbugyi200.athena.sase-p4.4 until epic sase-pv phase sase-pv.7 (migrate) deleted it on 2026-08-18. Feature flags are no longer their own bead type, so the old bead could not be converted in place -- the bead store's append-only guard makes `issue_type` immutable after `issue_created` -- and it was removed with `sase bead rm` and re-created here through `create_flag_bead`, the path `sase flag new` uses.

CARRIED OVER UNCHANGED: title, size (small), kind (beta), and both removal thresholds (2026-11-15 / 0.18.0). No deadline moved as a side effect of the migration.

AUTHORED FOR THE NEW REQUIRED FIELDS: `when_enabled`, `when_disabled`, and `remove_when` were drafted in the epic plan and each was verified against the code before it was written here. `src/sase/feature_flags/registry.py` now points `epic_resume_gate` at sase-qh.

SOAK sase-ru.3 2026-08-21: authored removal gate PASSES after a stall-clock fix.

Gap found on real artifacts: production failed done.json almost never has finished_at (sampled ~/.sase/projects/gh_sase-org__sase/artifacts/ace-run: 2613 done.json, 79 failed, typically finished_at=null). Example: agent sase-mg.land.w1--1 artifact 20260815194706 done.finished_at=null meta.stopped_at=2026-08-15T23:56:49.674861+00:00. stalled_epic requires finished_at, so the chop would never gate those real stalls.

Fix in this soak: build_done_marker now writes finished_at (unix epoch); sase_chop_epic_resume._member_finished_at prefers done.finished_at then agent_meta.stopped_at.

Operational evidence (isolated disposable project epic-soak, production scan_agent_artifacts + real EpicResume bundles, flag inherited via override_flags + apply_feature_flags_env → SASE_FEATURE_FLAGS):
- Settled stall (stopped_at 180s ago, settle_seconds=120, no done.finished_at): exactly one gate; second tick skipped. payload.clan_generation=20260821100000 resume_argv=["sase","bead","work",<epic>,"--yes-to-all"] action=EpicResume preview epic.md. pytest: tests/test_epic_resume_soak.py::test_historical_failed_phase_without_done_finished_at_raises_one_gate
- Fast retry (30s < 120s) and live handoff (live pid in newer generation 20260821110000): no gate.
- Recovery before settle: never gated.
- After gating, live member in newer generation cancels pending bundle (cancellation.json).
- Flag off: reason=flag_disabled, no bundle.
- Fakey non-retryable FAKEY-FAIL: phase crashed wrote genuine failed done.json with finished_at; chop gated at settle_seconds=0. pytest: tests/test_epic_resume_soak.py::test_fakey_failed_phase_gates_after_settle
- Unit: unreadable inventory/scan fail closed; repeated ticks skip; fingerprint re-gates; in-flight resume defers.

Removal-when: chop gated real (fakey + historical stopped_at) stalls without false positives on handoff races or fast retries at bead.epic_resume.settle_seconds=120.

Soak sase-ru.3 passed: fakey FAKEY-FAIL and historical stopped_at stalls raise one EpicResume gate; settle/handoff/fast-retry/recovery-before-settle produce no false positives; resume_argv is sase bead work. Removed the flag_disabled early return so gating is unconditional. Preserved settle window, fingerprint dedup, recovery cancellation, fail-closed inventory/scan, and notification priority. Retired registry/schema/help/docs Off-branch surfaces. Focused tests: 82 passed (chop, soak, gate, stall-policy, schema).
